# Get a cell number off call lists

Goal: remove the number from the lists that feed calls (not blocking calls on the phone).

First conversation: say in one line that you'll get their number off the lists telemarketers and robocallers buy. Then ask, one at a time:
1. The cell number, and their name and city/state (needed to match broker records).
2. OK to claim a dedicated bot email inbox for confirmation links.
Then start.

# Steps
1. National Do Not Call Registry: register at donotcall.gov, then open the confirmation email and click the link. Legit telemarketers must stop within 31 days.
2. Your state's Do Not Call list, if the state keeps a separate one.
3. Data brokers and people-search sites that sell numbers to marketers: file free official opt-outs for the number at FastPeopleSearch, TruePeopleSearch, USPhonebook, ThatsThem, Spokeo, Whitepages, BeenVerified, Nuwber, Intelius, PeopleFinders and similar. Many have a reverse-phone search; remove every listing tied to the number. Finish email confirmations from the bot inbox.
4. Marketing data lists: submit the DMAchoice (ANA) opt-out and the carrier's CPNI / marketing-sharing opt-out (Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile privacy settings).
5. Prescreened credit/insurance offers: optoutprescreen.com (the owner fills any SSN field themselves).
6. Report site by site what was filed and what's blocked (captcha, bot check). Explain that robocallers who ignore the law aren't stopped by lists; file complaints at donotcall.gov or reportfraud.ftc.gov for repeat callers.
7. Create a routine to recheck brokers every few months and refile where the number reappears.
Never pay or share the number beyond official opt-out forms without an explicit yes.
